title: Brian Schottenheimer on 105.3 The Fan | 9-24-26
headline: Coach says CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens could alternate as the featured option week to week, while Donovan Ezeiruaku is playing at a high level and Caleb Downs is getting involved early.
summary: Schottenheimer said the team is treating the trip to Baltimore like a short week, with the game plan finished before leaving so the staff can focus on acclimating. The group plans a Friday practice in Baltimore and a Saturday visit to the stadium, and he downplayed field concerns while saying the team has cleat options ready. On defense, the main task against Derrick Henry-type runners and Lamar Jackson is building a wall at the line and containing Jackson's movement, and he admitted the defense has not contained him well in the first two weeks. He said he handles motivation through one-on-one conversations and wants the team to keep improving through the early season. He said Kenny Clark is doing well and that the staff is managing rotations and play counts to keep the defensive line fresh. He praised Caleb Downs' practice habits and said Downs will be used early in games. He said CeeDee Lamb has been sharp in practice and that the Lamb and Pickens targets may swing from week to week. He also praised Donovan Ezeiruaku's pass-rush development and discussed Trey Hendrickson, the opposing edge rusher, as a matchup for Tyler Guyton.

signals.note: Lamb and Pickens may split the big-play and target share, so weekly volume is less predictable than usual.

signals.note: Pickens may have a week-to-week role that varies with CeeDee Lamb's performance.

signals.note: The staff wants Downs to be targeted and used early, which supports his impact even when his stat line is modest.

topics.detail: The team flew to Baltimore on Thursday after moving the schedule up to prepare on a short week. The plan includes Friday practice, a Saturday stadium visit, and sleep and acclimation focus.
Defensive priorities include stopping Derrick Henry-type runners and containing Lamar Jackson. Coach said the defense has to limit his movement and throws that can run past four or five seconds.
Coach commented on outside grading services such as PFF and Next Gen Stats, saying the coaching film evaluation matters more to him.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: September 24, 2026
headline: Saquon Barkley's status is unclear pending the injury report, Zach Ertz has not practiced yet, and Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley remain a trusted running back committee.
summary: Sirianni said the Bears are a strong, well-coached team and that the quarterback uncertainty is just another layer of weekly planning. He called the Eagles' 2026 season a process, with pads practice once a week, and emphasized block destruction and run defense as keys to this game. On takeaways, he said the team has had few real chances, since the opposing QBs have been mobile, and he stressed that tackling comes before strip attempts. He said Zach Ertz has not practiced yet and that trust is built through reps, so his readiness for Sunday will be determined at practice. On Saquon Barkley, he deferred to the injury report and said Barkley works hard to be ready each week. He praised Kenny Moore's competitiveness and said his versatility could let him contribute at safety, though it still needs to be seen in practice. He described Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley as a trusted committee at running back, both having earned reps, and he credited the depth after Barkley left a game. He also praised rookie Dontayvion Wicks's physicality, contested catching, and work ethic, saying the team saw his potential on tape before drafting him.

topics.detail: Sirianni said the uncertainty at QB adds planning layers, but every team faces a possible QB change each week, and the Eagles will follow their normal process.
Few takeaways so far because opposing QBs have been mobile. Sirianni said tackling comes first, and the team practices in pads once a week, with block destruction a focus.
Sirianni said the team does not focus on revenge. He praised the Bears' run game and their running back's one-cut ability, and said block destruction is the key to stopping it.

title: WATCH: Mike McCarthy Media Availability (Sept. 24)
headline: McCarthy praised Pat Freiermuth's play and said the offense needs more ball distribution, while promising DK Metcalf will get targets Sunday despite recent struggles.
summary: McCarthy said Asante Samuel Jr. has been consistent since day one of training camp, with two solid outings and a tough assignment this week. He was vague on an unnamed player (transcribed as 'Joey') who worked in a limited capacity, saying the player did the planned work and would be re-evaluated after more work Thursday. He said the Bengals' ability to stop the run without loading the box, including six-man front looks in the red zone, is being prepared for through situational work. On Aaron Rodgers, McCarthy said their conversations run longer because they have been apart for a while, and the staff is tailoring concepts to the perimeter players. He praised Patrick Graham's defensive staff for integrating players' individual skills into calls and in-game adjustments. McCarthy said Pat Freiermuth is playing well, has earned more opportunities, and he would like more ball distribution overall, including more targets for Freiermuth. On DK Metcalf, he said the team has support around him, the team will throw him the ball, and he will have opportunities Sunday. He described Wednesday's practice as the best of the year so far and said this is the next-to-last week of training camp.

injuries.detail: Limited in some capacity on Wednesday; he did the planned work and was scheduled for more work Thursday. McCarthy did not give a clear status.

signals.claim: Coach supports giving Freiermuth more targets and says he has earned more opportunities in the passing game
signals.note: Rodgers publicly wants more targets for him, and the coach agrees, which points to a larger role in the passing game.
signals.quote: Pat's playing really well. He's earned those opportunities.

signals.claim: Coach says Metcalf will get targets and opportunities in Sunday's game despite recent struggles
signals.note: The coach publicly committed to using him after a rough stretch, which supports his target share in Week 3.
signals.quote: You know we're going to throw the ball to DK.

signals.claim: Coach views Samuel as playing well and facing a big challenge this week
signals.note: Praise from the coach suggests a solid role at cornerback, but he is a defensive back with limited fantasy value.
signals.quote: He's been on the mark since, you know, day one.

topics.detail: McCarthy said Cincinnati has been productive stopping the run without loading the box, and the offense is preparing for four-man, five-man, and six-man front looks, especially in the red zone.
Rodgers' long history with McCarthy makes the weekly play-calling conversations longer. The staff is focused on concepts and variations that fit the perimeter players.
McCarthy credited the defensive staff for integrating players' skill sets into calls and in-game adjustments, and said communication has been strong.
McCarthy said corner depth is improving, with Daylen Everette cited for a strong competitive day and a special-teams role. The receiver group presents a huge challenge this week.
Wednesday was the best practice day of the year so far. McCarthy said the team will keep working different personnel combinations throughout the week.
